comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Fixed in 744edb6 (structured unknown fields kept typed; error on a tai field).

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A nested map in asset frontmatter is stringified with `%v` before it reaches the unknown-field path, so its value is mangled rather than kept or cleanly dropped.

```
---
name: demo
description: A demo skill
metadata:
  author: Someone
  tags:
    - a
    - b
version: 2
---
```

`frontmatter.Parse` gives:

```
metadata["metadata"] = "map[author:Someone tags:[a b]]"
metadata["version"]  = "2"
```

`Parsed.Metadata` is `map[string]string`, and the `default:` branch in `internal/frontmatter/frontmatter.go:134-139` runs `fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)` on anything that isn't a string. `native` keeps `map[string]any` and preserves nesting, so `native.claude` is unaffected.

In practice the damage is contained: an unknown field is dropped from the installed file with the decision-14 warning, which names the right fix.

```
Warning: skill "example": frontmatter field "metadata" is not a tai field and was not installed -
claude will not see it. Move it under 'native.claude' to pass it through in claude's own format.
```

So nothing mangled reaches a target today - the field that triggers this is exactly the field being dropped. What's left is a silent lossy conversion sitting in the parse path: any map-valued field tai later promotes to its own vocabulary would arrive as `map[...]`, and the stringification happens whether or not anything downstream wants it. Skills in the wild do carry `metadata:` (an external skill collection I install from has one, which is how I hit this), so the path runs regularly.

Keeping `rawMetadata` values typed past the parse, or special-casing `metadata` the way `depends`/`native` are, would both work. Worth a snapshot case with a nested map in frontmatter either way - the current tests don't cover one.

(Moved from GitHub issue #7.)
title: frontmatter: nested maps are stringified with %v instead of kept or dropped
